## OS-DEV-REPORT — #7495

**Outcome: `blocked` — premise broken. No code written, no PR opened.**

The card cannot be executed as written, for a reason that is not a judgement call: **there is no valid owner key for these three codes**, and registering them here reverses a separate, twice-confirmed maintainer ruling (#4805) that the card never addresses.

### The blocker, in the target file's own words

`error-code-ledger.zod.ts` opens with the #4805 scope rule (lines 19–54), a maintainer ruling of **2026-08-03, re-confirmed 2026-08-09** — two days *before* this card's ruling:

> Every owner key below is a package published from this repository, and that is a **RULE** … A downstream product repo (`objectstack-ai/cloud`, or any product built on the platform) does **not** register its codes here. It maintains its OWN ledger, in its own repo …
>
> **A commercial vocabulary does not belong in an Apache-2.0 spec.** The codes worth registering are precisely the product-specific ones (**billing and plan-gating states**, control-plane provisioning refusals) …
>
> … a PR adding an owner key for a package that is not published from this repository is **out of scope by construction**.

The three `AI_*` codes are cloud's plan-gating states — their CTAs are literally upgrade / top-up / trial. They are the paradigm case #4805 excludes.

**Mechanically:** `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` is keyed by *emitting package*, and the rows are provenance. I verified there is **no framework producer**: no AI/quota service exists anywhere in `packages/` (no `service-ai`, no matches for `aiAllowance` / `designQuota` / `dataChatTrial`), and the only repo-wide mentions of this vocabulary are the mirrored objectui changelog lines for `parseAiQuotaError`. Every candidate owner key would be fabricated. I could not pick one by default without asserting a provenance that does not exist.

**The seam is pinned in code**, not just prose. `contract.test.ts:588` (`makeApiErrorSchema (federated ledger, #4805)`) uses `DOWNSTREAM_CODES = ['CONTACT_SALES_PLAN', 'PRODUCTION_ENV_LIMIT']` — plan-gating literals of exactly this class — and asserts `ApiErrorSchema` **refuses** them, accepting them only through the downstream factory.

### Why I read this as an oversight, not an override

The 2026-08-11 ruling resolved a **shape** fork: closed literals vs `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` + structured `details`. Option A won on the merits recorded in the card — closed-enum literals are the hardest shape for AI consumers to misuse. **That verdict is untouched by #4805.** Option A is fully achievable with the ledger where #4805 put it:

```ts
// in cloud's own repo
const CloudApiError = makeApiErrorSchema(CLOUD_ERROR_CODES);  // StandardErrorCode ∪ cloud's ledger
```

The three literals stay closed, stay checkable, and objectui's `parseAiQuotaError` switches to the same three literals either way. The only thing that changes is **which repo's ledger declares them** — which is the exact question #4805 decided, and which this card's four-lens review does not appear to have had in front of it (the card cites neither #4805 nor an owner key). The filing seat was a triage Routine recording a ruling, which is the seat most likely to miss a cross-cutting rule.

### Reverse verification (predicted in writing, then run)

All probes on a throwaway copy in the worktree; **reverted, tree is clean, nothing committed.**

| # | Predicted | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| A | Adding the 3 codes under a framework owner key passes every gate — the violation is invisible to CI | **Confirmed.** 3 spec suites (`error-code-ledger`, `contract`, `error-catalog-docs`) 61/61 pass; `check-error-code-casing.mjs` green over 3576 files |
| B | Breaking casing fires the mechanical rule and names the offender | **Confirmed.** `× every registered code is SCREAMING_SNAKE` → `AssertionError: @objectstack/spec → AI_allowance_exhausted: expected 'AI_allowance_exhausted' to match /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$/` |
| C | Removing a row goes red on a completeness gate | **Refuted — and it is the file's own documented hole.** Deleting `MONGODB_MULTI_TENANT_UNSUPPORTED` left both suites green (58/58); the admission rules check casing/duplication/shadowing, never emittability (see the "Retiring a code" section, and #5783 / `OVERLAY_PERSISTENCE_FAILED`) |

**Probe A is the decisive one.** Landing this card would have gone green through CI with no reviewer signal that a standing ruling had been reversed. A silent green is precisely why I stopped instead of shipping it.
